deep.reconstruction:
This page continues Grothendieck's 1953 draft on what he calls 'espaces de Schatten': operator ideals on Hilbert spaces E, F defined by a symmetric norming function N on finitely supported sequences.

Setup (previous page). For compact u, put N(u) = N((λ_i(u))), where λ_i(u) are the singular values. For arbitrary bounded u, put N(u) = sup |Tr(uw)| over finite-rank w with N°(w) ≤ 1, where N° is the polar (dual) norming function. Then L^N is the set of u with N(u) < ∞, and L_N is the closure of the finite-rank operators E'⊗F in L^N.

The page proves or announces the following.
(1) Corollary. N(u) = N(|u|). For the Cartesian decomposition u = h + ik one has N(u) ≤ N(h) + N(k), so u ∈ L^N iff h, k ∈ L^N.
(2) Proposition. L^N(E,F) ⊂ L_0(E,F), the compact operators, unless N is equivalent to N_∞; in that case L^N = L(E,F). Proof:
- If |u| is not compact, a spectral projection of |u| has infinite rank and |u| ≥ εP on it.
- So v = f(|u|) is a hermitian operator with v|u| = P, an infinite-rank orthogonal projection. By the ideal property, P ∈ L^N.
- Testing P against diagonal finite-rank w gives Σ|x_i| ≤ M·N°(x). Hence N° is equivalent to N_1, so N is equivalent to N_∞, a contradiction.
(3) Corollary. L^{N_p} = L^p, the Schatten p-classes. For p < ∞, L_{N_p} = L^{N_p}.
(4) Hölder-type pairing. u ∈ L^N and v ∈ L^{N°} imply vu is trace class. This gives a trace duality between L^N(E,F) and L^{N°}(F,E).
(5) Duality. The dual of L_N is L^{N°}. Consequently:
- L^N and L_N are complete.
- L_N is reflexive if N is reflexive, with the converse when E and F are infinite-dimensional.
- L_N is reflexive iff L^N is reflexive.
- For 1 < p < ∞, L^p is reflexive with dual L^{p'}.
(6) Generalized Hölder. If N(xy) ≤ N'(x)N''(y) on sequences, then N(vu) ≤ N'(u)N''(v). The proof reduces to finite-dimensional compressions p_ν u p_ν, using N(u) = lim N(p u p) and the known finite-dimensional theorem (a convexity theorem; crossed-out attempts mention a three-factor version). He also remarks that the inequality can be made sharp (equality attained).
(7) Two items are only announced: an inequality comparing N or N° of a sequence built from u with N(u), and a characterization of Schatten norms.

Purpose: a systematic theory of symmetrically normed ideals, as a chapter feeding the theory of tensor products and nuclear operators.
errors: The duality statement as written, 'dual of L_N(E,F) is L^N(E,F)', must mean L^{N°}(F,E). This is consistent with the trace pairing stated just above it and with the l_N / l^{N°} duality on the previous page.
In the compactness proof the transcription has Σ|x_i|^2 ≤ M; the argument requires Σ|x_i| ≤ M·N°(x), giving N° ≈ N_1. This is either a slip or a misreading.
In the generalized Hölder proposition the target space is written L^N(E,F) rather than L^N(E,G); the order N'(u)N''(v) versus N'(v)N''(u) also fluctuates between this page and the next.
The finite-dimensional step is not argued; it is cited as known. It holds via Horn's inequality (weak log-majorization of singular values of vu) plus Ky Fan dominance.
The final 'Prop N°((λ_i(u))) ≤ N(u)' is unclear as transcribed. It is probably a statement about a sequence of diagonal entries or eigenvalues being dominated by N(u).

ideas.what: Symmetrically normed operator ideals L^N, L_N built from a symmetric norming function N; extension to all bounded operators via a trace-duality sup
ideas.modern_name: Symmetrically normed ideals / Schatten–von Neumann norm ideals (S_Φ and S_Φ^(0))
ideas.usually_credited_to: von Neumann (1937, symmetric gauge functions), Schatten (1950, 1960), Calkin (1941); systematized by Gohberg–Krein (1965)
ideas.where_published: Possibly touched on in Produits tensoriels topologiques (1955), Ch. II; unsure

ideas.what: L^N contained in the compact operators unless N is equivalent to the sup norm, proved via an infinite spectral projection
Dual of L_N is L^{N°} under trace pairing; reflexivity of L_N iff reflexivity of the sequence space
ideas.modern_name: Duality and reflexivity of symmetrically normed ideals

ideas.what: Generalized Hölder inequality N(vu) ≤ N'(u)N''(v) from the scalar inequality N(xy) ≤ N'(x)N''(y), by finite-dimensional reduction
ideas.modern_name: Hölder inequality for symmetric norm ideals (Horn / Ky Fan majorization)

missed.claim: In 1953 Grothendieck had a full abstract treatment of norm ideals built from arbitrary symmetric norming functions: definition via trace duality, duality L_N' = L^{N°}, the reflexivity criterion and a general Hölder inequality. This predates Schatten's 'Norm Ideals of Completely Continuous Operators' (1960) and Gohberg–Krein (1965). It is a priority/historical detail, not a new mathematical result.
missed.quote: Prop Si N,N',N'' sont des normes de Schatten telles que N(xy)≤N'(x)N''(y), alors u∈L^{N'}(E,F), v∈L^{N''}(F,G) implique vu∈L^N
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's independent early development of symmetrically normed ideals, relevant to histories of operator ideals (Pietsch, Gohberg–Krein). No mathematical content appears new.

deep.surprise_reason: The material is now standard (symmetrically normed ideals, duality, Hölder). The only point of interest is that Grothendieck worked it out in 1953, before the Schatten 1960 and Gohberg–Krein syntheses; this is a mild priority note.
transcription_corrections: The proof inequality should likely read 'Σ|x_i| ≤ M' (the image shows 'Σ|x_i|' followed by an unclear mark), not Σ|x_i|^2.
The margin note at the top-left is a question about L_N(E,F), likely 'A-t-on ... = L_N(E,F)?'
'N(vu)=lim N(p_ν u p)' is more plausibly 'N(u)=lim_p N(p u p)=lim_p N(u_p)'.
'Par propriétés asth.' is likely 'Par propriétés connues des espaces de dimension finie' (or similar).
